RESPECT ALDUIN

Alduin, the World-Eater, First Born of Akatosh.

BIOGRAPHY:

Alduin is known to the residents of Skyrim as an immensely powerful dragon. He is depicted as a malevolent force who casually destroys the world periodically. The Nords of Skyrim believe that his reappearance heralds the end of time.

Alduin's name can be separated into "Al Du In", which means "Destroyer Devour Master" in Dragon Tongue.

FEATS:

  • Can attack via Ice Breath, this form of attack is a weakened form of Alduin that's also nerfed by gameplay.

  • Casually beats up Mehrunes Dagon, multiple times.

"Yeah, sure," Aless giggled, "And how does that work out for you? Every single fight you have with the Dragon ends up with you losing, King Chump[1]. And it will always be like that. Here, there, then, now, or in the future: the Dragon wins over you, as he wins over us all. I'm not afraid of that anymore. More importantly, I'm not afraid of YOU."

[1] King Chump refers to Mehrunes Dagon.

  • When summoned by Orkey, he eats almost every nord over the age of six

Seeing the strength of King Wulfharth, Orkey summoned the ghost of Alduin Time-Eater again. Nearly every Nord was eaten down to six years old.

  • Eats Mehrunes Dagon

After many looks east, west, south, and north, and seeing only the churning dragon stop around him, Dagon realized that at some point when he was begging with his eyes closed that Alduin had eaten him, mountaintop and all,

  • Can bring dragons back to life

Attack on Titan

Genres: Action, Drama, Fantasy, Horror, Psychological Thriller

Episode Count: 25 + 2 OVA

Studio: WIT Studio

Director: Tetsuro Araki

Music: Hiroyuki Sawano

Air Time: April 6, 2013 – September 28, 2013

Additional Materials: Movie (2015), Manga (2009 - Present), Video Game (2014)

Several hundred years ago, humans were nearly exterminated by giants. Giants are typically several stories tall, seem to have no intelligence, devour human beings and, worst of all, seem to do it for the pleasure rather than as a food source. A small percentage of humanity survived by enclosing themselves in a city protected by extremely high walls, even taller than the biggest of giants. Flash forward to the present and the city has not seen a giant in over 100 years. Teenage boy Eren and his foster sister Mikasa witness something horrific as the city walls are destroyed by a super giant that appears out of thin air. As the smaller giants flood the city, the two kids watch in horror as their mother is eaten alive. Eren vows that he will murder every single giant and take revenge for all of mankind.

(Quick info from: Anime News Network )

Why was it hyped up?

Because people die when they are killed (and actually stay dead this time). With the perception that 'no character is safe', many people saw this as a breakthough in shounen anime in which unbridled optimism is often the norm. Attack on Titan is so popular that it is considered the latest trigger for an influx of anime watchers and is a 'first anime' for many people.

I had heard great things about this show, and I went into it with high expectations. The unique art style and setting did not disappoint, and a catchy & memorable OP didn't hurt either. However, I immediately noticed that the pacing was incredibly slow. I made it through the first few episodes, hoping it would pick up after a bit. Unfortunately, I reached the infamous boulder arc and the already slow pacing screeched to a halt. Bad pacing can definitely kill a series for me, and this one fell victim to it. I also feel that Eren's secret was revealed far too early in the series, and it could have been much better revealed later on.

So overall, no, it did not live up to the hype, at least for me. I expected an energetic adventure involving fighting the titans, but I instead got a slow paced story that did not really do much for me.

Once-theoretical crypto attack against HTTPS now verges on practicality (x-post v/technology)

By observing roughly 9227 encryptions of the cookie, the attacker can guess the contents with 94 percent accuracy. With the ability to make the target transmit 4,450 Web requests per second, the attack takes about 75 hours, although in some cases, the time required can be shaved down to 52 hours. In the attack from two years ago, researchers required 12230 encryptions of a cookie to deduce its contents and could generate only about 1,700 requests per second.

The new attack against WPA-TKIP requires an hour to execute, and allows an attacker to inject and decrypt arbitrary packets.
